moments.title: De revolutionibus published
moments.body:
Copernicus's heliocentric model is published in the year of his death.

Its mathematics is comparable in complexity to Ptolemy's, but it places the Sun at the centre.
moments.takeaway: A simpler conceptual model was, in calculation, no simpler than its rival.

moments.title: Galileo's telescope observations
moments.body:
Galileo's improved telescope reveals lunar craters, Jupiter's moons, Venus's phases and sunspots.

The phases of Venus are direct evidence against Ptolemy's system.
moments.takeaway: An instrument decided a centuries-long debate.

moments.title: Newton's Principia
moments.body: Newton derives planetary motion from universal gravitation. The Royal Society publishes the Principia at Edmond Halley's expense.
moments.takeaway: Empirical celestial mechanics and a single mathematical framework unified.

now.title: Cosmology today
now.body: General relativity, expansion of space and standard cosmological model frame current research. Open problems include dark matter, dark energy and the Hubble tension.
now.open_questions: What is dark energy? Why do different methods give different values for the Hubble constant?

items.reflection: Heliocentrism is now intuitive in education; in 1600 it was an institutional fight that destroyed careers.

moments.title: Lemaitre derives the expansion
moments.body: Lemaitre publishes the relationship between redshift and distance in French two years before Hubble's English paper.
moments.takeaway: Language and venue affected credit for what is now the Hubble-Lemaitre Law.

moments.title: Hubble's paper
moments.body: Hubble's English-language paper presents distance-redshift data for nearby galaxies, supporting cosmic expansion.
moments.takeaway: Observation and theory met in different journals and languages.

moments.title: Cosmic microwave background discovered
moments.body: Penzias and Wilson detect a uniform microwave signal initially treated as noise. Dicke's Princeton group identifies it as the relic radiation predicted by Big Bang cosmology.
moments.takeaway: Major theoretical predictions can be verified accidentally.

now.title: Modern cosmology
now.body: Precision measurements from WMAP, Planck and surveys like DES refine cosmological parameters. JWST and the Vera Rubin Observatory will extend the data baseline.
now.open_questions: Why is matter so unevenly distributed? Will the Hubble tension be resolved by new physics or systematics?

items.reflection: Cosmology has shifted from a speculative branch of astronomy to a precision science within a single human lifetime.

moments.title: Hubble Space Telescope launched
moments.who: NASA and ESA, Space Shuttle Discovery
moments.body:
Hubble launches with a flawed primary mirror. The 1993 servicing mission corrects the optics.

Hubble produces transformative deep-field images and exoplanet atmosphere data.
moments.takeaway: Space-based observatories combine extraordinary capability with risky logistics.

moments.title: First exoplanet around a sunlike star
moments.who: Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz, Geneva
moments.body: 51 Pegasi b is detected by radial velocity. Mayor and Queloz share the 2019 Nobel Prize in Physics.
moments.takeaway: Astronomy's exoplanet era began with a single detection.

moments.title: JWST launch and first images
moments.body: JWST launches on 25 December 2021 and releases its first science images on 12 July 2022.
moments.takeaway: A 30-year project produced data that immediately reshaped early-universe astronomy.

now.title: Observatories today
now.body: JWST, Vera Rubin Observatory and ESO's Extremely Large Telescope (under construction) push deeper across wavelengths. Space-based gravitational wave detectors are planned.
now.open_questions: How early can JWST trace galaxy formation? What can we learn about exoplanet atmospheres?

items.reflection: Major instruments depend on decadal planning and international collaboration in scientific bodies that are increasingly under political strain.

moments.title: Zwicky on cluster mass
moments.body: Zwicky's analysis of the Coma cluster requires far more mass than visible to explain the velocities of galaxies, coining 'dunkle Materie'.
moments.takeaway: Early evidence for dark matter was overlooked for decades.

moments.title: Rubin's flat rotation curves
moments.body: Rotation curves of spiral galaxies stay flat at large radii, implying substantial unseen mass.
moments.takeaway: Direct kinematic measurements made dark matter unavoidable.

moments.title: Accelerating expansion
moments.body: Type Ia supernova observations indicate the expansion of the universe is accelerating, inviting the term 'dark energy'.
moments.takeaway: Two of three independent observations changed the cosmic budget.

now.title: Dark sector today
now.body: About 27% of the universe is modelled as dark matter and 68% as dark energy. Direct detection experiments (e.g. LZ, XENONnT) and surveys (DESI, Euclid) seek further constraints.
now.open_questions: Are dark matter and dark energy single phenomena? Could modifications of gravity replace them?

items.reflection: Most of the universe's energy budget is described by negative results: things we have not detected directly.
